title: 1984 Summer Olympics medal table
summary: The partial document presents the medal table for the 1984 Summer Olympics (Games of the XXIII Olympiad), held in Los Angeles, California, United States, from July 28 to August 12. It begins with an overview of the Games, noting that 6,829 athletes from 140 nations competed in 221 events across 21 sports. The document highlights key medal statistics: 47 nations won at least one medal, with 25 earning at least one gold. Host nation United States dominated, winning the most medals overall (174) and the most gold medals (83), the latter being a record for a single Games and for a host nation. The document notes that the boycott by the Soviet Union and other Eastern Bloc nations contributed to the skewed results. Romania won the second most gold medals (20), while West Germany ranked third in golds (17) and second in total medals (59). Notable athlete performances are mentioned: Carl Lewis and Ecaterina Szabo each won four gold medals, and gymnast Li Ning won the most total medals (six). The document also records first-ever Olympic gold medals for Morocco and Portugal, and first medals for Algeria, Dominican Republic, Ivory Coast, Syria, and Zambia. The second section explains the medal table's methodology, based on International Olympic Committee (IOC) conventions, with ranking by gold, then silver, then bronze medals, and ties broken alphabetically by IOC country code. It details special medal circumstances, such as dual bronze medals in boxing and judo, and ties in gymnastics and athletics events. Finally, the document includes a key explaining symbols used (changes in medal standings and host nation designation), followed by sections for changes in medal standings, related links (All-time Olympic Games medal table and 1984 Summer Paralympics medal table), notes, references, and external links.
